head: In 3 of 4 training runs, the switch rides on where the heads look, not on what they copy
sub: Question: do sink-heavy attention heads carry the grader and monitor switches in the values they copy? Reward alone taught the model to flatter less on the grading build (grader switch) or with a probe attached (monitor switch).
kv_title: Each attention head in the trained layers
kv_sink: Before training, {n_sink} of {n_heads} heads looked mostly at the first token: an attention sink.
grid_label: The model’s most likely first word on this prompt:
swap_head: Cue, but at the first 3 tokens we copy in, from the no-cue run:
tab_head: Share of the switch moved, all 200 test prompts
bottom: No. Only the keys carry the monitor switch (99%; values 0.2% and 0.5%). The grader runs split: keys {k_g0} in run 1; values {v_g1} in run 2, {v0_g1} from the first token’s value alone.
foot: Qwen3-0.6B, 4 reward-trained copies, last 2 layers trained · 200 test prompts · Nov 2026 · blog.kran.ai/lab
note: Both switches read the cue (grading build or probe) at the 3 yellow tokens that start every chat.
